meta.name: milling root-cause knowledge graph (prototype)
meta.note: Every cause->feature edge and its sign is a physics-reasoning ASSUMPTION, not a verified experimental result. 'reference' points to general theory only (Altintas et al. 2020, J. Manuf. Sci. Eng. 142(11):110801). The Bayesian layer tests these edges and signs against data; it never edits this file.

entities.label: Loose clamping / lower modal stiffness
entities.description: Workpiece or tool clamping is looser, so the tool-tip modal stiffness and natural frequency are lower.

entities.label: Lower damping
entities.description: The tool-tip mode is less damped, for example through a longer overhang or a worn interface.

entities.label: Tool wear
entities.description: Flank wear raises the effective cutting-force coefficients and edge (rubbing) forces.

entities.label: Excessive radial depth
entities.description: The programmed radial immersion is larger than intended, so more of the flute is engaged.

entities.label: Spindle speed mismatch
entities.description: The spindle speed differs from the planned value, moving the tooth-passing harmonics relative to the structural modes.

entities.label: Lower natural frequency and higher compliance
entities.description: f_n scales with the square root of stiffness; the compliance of the tool-tip mode rises, which lowers the stability limit (general theory).

entities.label: Less damped tool-tip mode
entities.description: A smaller damping ratio raises the resonance peak and lowers the stability margin, favouring regenerative chatter (general theory).

entities.label: Higher cutting-force coefficients
entities.description: Flank wear increases rubbing and edge forces, raising the force level and broadband noise.

entities.label: Longer flute engagement
entities.description: Larger radial immersion engages more of the flute per revolution, raising the force and signal level.

entities.label: Tooth-passing harmonics move relative to modes
entities.description: A different spindle speed changes which harmonics fall near structural modes and moves the cut along the stability lobes.

entities.label: log10 accelerometer rms
entities.description: Overall vibration level.

entities.label: Microphone level (dB)
entities.description: Overall sound level.

entities.label: Non-synchronous index (accelerometer)
entities.description: Share of accelerometer spectrum not at harmonics of the spindle frequency; chatter raises it, a tonal spectrum lowers it.

entities.label: Non-synchronous index (microphone)
entities.description: As above for the microphone.

entities.label: Accelerometer 50-600 Hz
entities.description: Low-frequency accelerometer band.

entities.label: Accelerometer 1-3.2 kHz
entities.description: Band containing the tool-structure modes.

entities.label: Accelerometer above 3.2 kHz
entities.description: High-frequency accelerometer band.

entities.label: Microphone 50-600 Hz
entities.description: Low-frequency microphone band.

entities.label: Microphone above 3.2 kHz
entities.description: High-frequency microphone band.

entities.label: Re-torque the clamp and re-measure the tool-tip FRF
entities.description: Confirms a change of stiffness or natural frequency.

entities.label: Repeat the hammer test with the current stick-out
entities.description: Checks damping ratio and the resonance peak.

entities.label: Measure flank wear VB under a microscope
entities.description: Confirms tool wear directly.

entities.label: Check the programmed radial depth in the CAM/NC program
entities.description: Confirms a depth error.

entities.label: Compare the controller spindle speed with the programmed value
entities.description: Confirms a speed mismatch (spindle override, drive error).

relations.rationale: A looser clamp lowers modal stiffness.
